correctness.rationale: The proof begins with exact reduced source equations. The feasible simplex is invariant and (x+y+z)′=-ηz gives an integrable infected compartment with z→0. The susceptible sum has a limit and the scalar stable x-filter gives both coordinate limits. Gronwall proves positivity of the final susceptible mass. If r x∞>1, the infected class would eventually grow exponentially, contradicting integrability; hence the endpoint belongs to the source stable segment. For balanced infected seeds, x≤u and z≤δ exp[-η(1-ru)t] are rigorous global comparison inequalities. Their integrable envelope proves the sharp derivative by dominated convergence and continuity of the endpoint map. Intermediate-value bracketing then constructs an exactly convergent infected trajectory for every open-segment target. Density of all target limits forces each closed attracting set to contain the entire stable segment. The scope carefully excludes unseeded invariant equilibria.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic final-size monotonicity and minimal equilibrium attractors for SIR are conceptual prior art and are not claimed as novel. The proof uses the special s=x+y dissipation, its stable x-filter, and a q-dependent sharp perturbation coefficient.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2024 primary article explicitly marks complete stable-endpoint coverage and smallest attracting set as a numerical conjecture (Section 5.2/Fig. 12), despite an existing one-way terminal-set theorem and conditional asymptotic-stability result. The new proof establishes exact endpoint reachability, closure-minimal attraction on the infected sector, and the exact first-order weak-seed loss. The 2020 source model paper is a simulation and parameter-fitting study. A 2022 SIR-model minimal-attractor theorem is acknowledged as close conceptual prior, but it does not imply the reversible-confined susceptible exchange model with q>0 or its sharp response coefficient. No searched or inspected source gives this complete result for the motivating three-dimensional model.
residual_risks: Some broader SIR control papers were available only through indexed full-text excerpts, not all appendices; an unindexed general theorem on reversible quarantine remains possible.
The exact terminal value map away from the balanced-seed family is not expressed in closed form; the source confinement-tonicity integral remains relevant.
The closed stable segment is not an attracting set for every initial state in the full simplex when unseeded unstable equilibria exist; the accepted theorem deliberately uses the infected sector.
The infinitesimal-seed expansion is nonuniform near the invasion threshold.

value.rationale: This resolves an explicitly named 2024 published numerical conjecture about whether final outbreak outcomes span the entire stable equilibrium segment. It is a complete, natural endpoint-reachability classification for a biologically motivated reversible-quarantine model, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The proof additionally quantifies how weak imported infection depletes susceptibles and exhibits the precise sensitivity to baseline epidemic pressure and confinement ratio. The statement distinguishes seeded trajectories from disease-free stationary points, a boundary essential for interpreting smallest-attractor claims.
